removed_uncertainties.text: Lines 1–2: חִפַּשְׂנֻהוּ, מְצָאנֻהוּ, יְדַעֲנֻהוּ, הִכַּרְנֻהוּ. Each could be qubuts or shuruq-vav. הִכַּרְנֻהוּ is the least certain.
Line 3, יוּכַל: the vowel under the kaf could be patah or qamatz, and the vav could carry holam.
Line 13, כַּמִּיּוֹת: the consonants are כמיות, but the pointing is unclear.
Line 14, כַּבּוֹרֵא: the first letter could be kaf or bet. The footnote paraphrase on s341 has 'בבורא'.
Line 14, בְּרָאָם: the dagesh is uncertain.
Line 6, בְּבִינָה פְּעָלָם: I can't confirm the dageshim.
Line 12: the * is the footnote mark printed above כָּל. It is not part of the poem text.
Line 11, נְחַשְׁבֵהוּ: the sheva under the nun is visible, but a dagesh in the shin is possible.
Line 2, 'המפרשים': in this Rashi face shin and samekh look alike to me. Context and the other shins on the page (שער, שבעה, ששה) support shin.
Line 7, 'הכמות ,והאיכות': there is a comma-like mark before the vav, kept as printed. It may be a stray mark.
Line 17, 'נחר ומותך': I can't read the first word. It could begin with nun or gimel.
'והמאמרים' (Averroes's list of quantities) is clear in the image.
Line 4, 'פ״י': I'm reasonably confident in this reading.
